name: Saʿd al-Dīn Masʿūd ibn ʿUmar al-Taftāzānī
summary: The Khurasanian master of the madrasa sciences, whose first book, written in his youth, was the commentary on al-Zanjānī's al-ʿIzzī that the Ottoman madrasas read as 'Saʿd al-Dīn'.
bio: Al-Taftāzānī was born in Taftāzān near Nasā in Khurasan in 722/1322 and studied with ʿAḍud al-Dīn al-Ījī and Quṭb al-Dīn al-Rāzī's circle. He taught in Herat, Khwārazm and Sarakhs and spent his last years at Tīmūr's court in Samarqand, where he died in 792/1390.

His Sharḥ al-Taṣrīf al-ʿIzzī is, by the reports, his first work, finished in 738/1338 when he was sixteen; it explains al-Zanjānī's al-ʿIzzī phrase by phrase and was read with it in the Ottoman madrasas as part of the ṣarf course. His later books on rhetoric (al-Muṭawwal and al-Mukhtaṣar on al-Qazwīnī's Talkhīṣ), logic (Tahdhīb al-manṭiq) and theology made him one of the most read authors of the madrasa, and his Irshād al-hādī is a short naḥw.
uncertain: His death is also given as 791 or 793; the age at which he wrote the commentary on al-ʿIzzī comes from the biographers.
